expectation: Nuclear KLF2 in endothelial cells lining vessels (thin rings around lumens), and in naive/quiescent T cells, which cluster in lymphoid aggregates and T zones. Expect a distinct subset of nuclei that are bright, with stroma dim.
observed: A: haze over the whole slide, with banding and glow off the tissue and bright specks scattered on the glass. B and C: diffuse stromal/ECM glow with nuclei-rich bands dimmer, and no stained nuclei. D: haze, no cells. E1: uniform grain over the whole field. E3 overlap follows CD3E density.
why: The signal is haze and grain that follows tissue texture and the background, with no distinct population of KLF2-positive nuclei at any scale.
notes: KLF2 glows over stroma and background, including off-tissue gradients and speckle, while nuclear regions are dimmer. No vessel-lining or T-cell nuclei stand out. Row E is uniform grain, so its white overlap reflects how dense the cells are, not specific co-staining.
